 HONOLULU (KHON2) -- The first printout results are in for the Hawaii General Election. Here's where candidates for U.S. House Hawaii District 2, Jill Tokuda and Brenton Awa, stand right now.
 Tokuda is ahead with 97,049 and Awa is trailing behind at 39,224.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Incumbent Democrat Tokuda and Republican Awa will face off for a seat in the U.S. House of Representatives.
 Here's what to know about this year's race to represent Hawaii's second Congressional District.
  STAY UPDATED: More Hawaii Elections 2026 coverage  
 Tokuda is running for re-election and Awa, who currently serves as a member of the Hawaii State Senate District 23, is aiming to step into the position.
 The seat represents Hawaii Island, Kauai, Maui, Lanai, Molokai Niihau, Kahoolawe, the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands and suburban and rural parts of Oahu.
 In 2023, Tokuda took on the role as Hawaii's 2nd District U.S. Representative. She previously served District 24, including Kaneohe and Kailua, at the Hawaii State Senate from 2006 to 2018.
 Advertisement Advertisement To learn more about Tokuda and her campaign, click HERE .
 On Awa's website, he said, "No one should have to choose between leaving the place they love, and building the life they deserve."
 Awa was elected to the State Senate in 2022, representing District 23, which is comprised of Kaneohe, Kahaluu, Laie, Kahuku, Mokuleia, Schofield Barracks and Kunia Camp.
 For more information on Awa and his campaign, click HERE .
  Click Here: 2026 Hawaii General Election Race Results  
 Both candidates are running to combat affordability issues, including housing and health care.
 To vote, you must cast your ballot before 7 p.m. on Nov. 3.
